flags.message: MCP courtlistener_search returned HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded. Relied on snapshot and base rates.
Used a web search to gather context on the pending dispute. The case has not yet been decided by the Supreme Court.

The frozen context records amicus_briefs as 0, but the provisioned August 18 snapshot visibly lists six amicus submissions (one on August 16 and five on August 18). The amicus-increment probability is stated against the harness-owned frozen zero, as required, while the prose separately notes that few or no filings beyond the six visible are expected.

The truncated snapshot's undated Other-counsel block lists multiple nonparties although the dated proceedings and frozen context record zero amicus briefs. Because truncated snapshots can retain undated blocks as of the later pull, I treated that block as potentially post-cutoff and did not use it to resolve the amicus-increment claim.

Frozen context reads amicus_briefs: 0 while the provisioned 2026-08-18 snapshot visibly carries six amicus filings. Cause: the amicus counter (interim_signals._AMICUS_RE) matches the literal phrase 'amicus curiae', but this application docket's entries read 'Amicus brief of X submitted.' and never contain it. The undercount hits both ends of the amicus-increment claim (frozen state and resolution-time signal), so the claim will likely resolve false despite real, possibly growing amicus activity, and the statpack's interim amicus escalation counts are likewise undercounted for dockets using this entry style. My amicus-increment probability (0.10) prices the measurement, not the world.

Frozen context says amicus_briefs: 0, but the truncated snapshot's attorney roster already lists six non-party 'Other' counsel of the amicus-filing kind (Members of Congress/CAC, Society for the Rule of Law, Campaign Legal Center/CREW, State of Indiana, two individuals) — the roster appears to reflect post-cutoff appearances while the proceedings list is cut at 2026-08-15. I resolved my amicus-increment claim against the frozen zero per the contract; noting in case the roster/counter skew affects other cells.

Decisive forward signal from outside the snapshot: CourtListener retrieval of D.C. Circuit docket 26-5123 showed the 2026-08-07 per curiam judgment affirming the preliminary injunction (Rao dissenting), with the ruling self-stayed 14 days for Supreme Court review and the mandate reset to 2026-08-21. This predates the 2026-08-15 snapshot cutoff and drove my adjustment up from the pooled 13.3% baseline. Retrieval was stopped short of anything that could surface the application's own disposition; I did not encounter it.

The harness-frozen context records amicus_briefs=2, but the provisioned snapshot lists five distinct amicus filings dated August 3, 2026. I used the frozen count as the declared claim baseline but did not treat already-visible filings as future increments; mechanical resolution of amicus-increment may therefore encode a provisioning/parser mismatch.

Frozen context reports amicus_briefs=2 while the snapshot shows five amicus filings: interim_signals._AMICUS_RE matches the singular 'amicus curiae' only, so the three entries styled 'amici curiae' (56 Former Judges; Bipartisan Former Governors; Asian Law Caucus, et al.) are not counted. Internally consistent for the amicus-increment claim (the same counter resolves it), but the count understates amicus interest on any docket where filers docket in the plural form, which is most multi-filer briefs.

Three of the five amicus entries carry 'VIDED', which normally marks a filing docketed across companion applications, yet the snapshot's RelatedCaseNumber is empty and a metadata-restricted CourtListener search surfaced no companion SCOTUS application from the federal defendants. Whether the enjoined federal parties have a parallel application materially affects this application's grant probability; the record available to this cell cannot resolve it.

Forward-mode web retrieval used a decisive companion signal: the Solicitor General's parallel stay application in the same litigation (26A124, filed 2026-07-27, pre-cutoff), plus press coverage of the underlying injunction. One surfaced headline post-dated the cutoff (a 2026-08-12 report of another injunction in parallel mail-voting litigation); it did not disclose this application's own disposition, was not opened, and no post-cutoff outcome material was folded into the forecast.

The truncated snapshot's attorney roster appears to reflect capture-time state rather than the 2026-07-30 cutoff: it lists counsel for five amicus groups while the truncated proceedings show no amicus entries and the frozen context has amicus_briefs=0. I used the roster as signal for the amicus-increment claim; if the roster postdates the cutoff, that claim's evidence base is mildly post-cutoff for a forward cell (harmless here, but the seam may matter for replay provisioning).

A parallel federal-defendants' application in the same matter exists as its own corpus case (scotus/9526000124); I learned of it from a committed sibling prediction read for field conventions and used its existence and mid-August pendency as forward signal. Separately: this application's response was due 2026-08-03 and the run is 2026-08-20, so a disposition likely exists by now; I did not retrieve either SCOTUS docket's post-cutoff state and do not know the outcome (all CourtListener docket queries bounded to entries on/before 2026-07-29).

The frozen context records distribution_count=1, but the snapshot's only distribution (May 19, for the June 4 conference) predates the paid petition's August 6 docketing and appears to concern linked miscellaneous matter 25M81 and the veteran-status motion denied June 8. The petition itself was not yet due a response until September 8. I preserved the harness-frozen count when forecasting relist-increment, so that claim is high because the petition's expected first real distribution will mechanically increase the count; it should not be interpreted as a forecast of a true relist.

The frozen distribution_count of 1 reflects the May 19, 2026 distribution (Conference of 6/4/2026), which belongs to the case's miscellaneous-docket motion phase (linked 25M81) and predates the petition's August 6, 2026 docketing as 26-173 — the docket's proceedings list carries the pre-docketing entries with out-of-order dates (petition entry dated Mar 19, distribution May 19, docketed Aug 6). The relist-increment claim is stated from the frozen count of 1 as required, but the petition proper has not yet been distributed, so the increment's baseline state conflates the motion's conference with the petition's.

The event file was present, but the workflow-provisioned record directory was absent: no snapshot, context.json, documents.json, or filed-document text was available. The prediction therefore uses committed aggregate base rates plus the event caption only; no live case docket was retrieved.

Frozen distribution_count=1 counts the June 10, 2026 distribution of the sealing motion (25M91) for the 6/25/2026 conference, not a distribution of the petition itself — the petition has never been conferenced (BIO due Aug 26, 2026, after this snapshot). The baseline band and my relist-increment claim are stated from that count as frozen; if the resolver counts only petition distributions the increment claim is unaffected (a first petition distribution is near-certain either way), but the band may understate the petition's eventual trajectory.

This case (the 9/11 military-commission plea-agreement mandamus litigation) was widely covered through the model's training cutoff, including the D.C. Circuit's July 2025 decision and the January 2026 en banc denial. The cert petition's disposition post-dates the cutoff and the docket confirms it is pending, so no outcome knowledge exists; background familiarity was used only as pre-snapshot public context.

Forward-signal disclosure: web search (2026-08-20) for the companion state case Baxter v. Philadelphia Board of Elections (Pa.) showed it argued September 2025 with no decision yet. That pending state-constitutional challenge is the BIO's lead vehicle/mootness argument and materially shaped this forecast (it is the main reason P(grant) is 0.55 rather than higher). Nothing about this petition's own disposition was sought or surfaced; none can exist yet post-CVSG.
The questions-presented.txt file contains text from the body of the petition instead of the actual Questions Presented. I extracted the QP directly from petition.txt using grep.

The provisioned questions-presented.txt contains an excerpt from the petition's importance section rather than the questions presented. Both questions were recoverable from the intact petition.txt and brief-in-opposition.txt, so the cell could finish.

questions-presented.txt does not carry the petition's QP section: it opens mid-sentence inside the 'Reasons for Granting the Petition' part ("In This Case Are Exceptionally Important..."). The actual questions presented were recovered from the provisioned petition.txt, so the cell was unaffected, but the QP extractor mis-cut this document.

Corpus query surface was unusable in this cell: two fedcourts query attempts timed out against the corpus service (180s ReadTimeout on the first, a 100s wrapper kill on the second) and returned no rows. The cell degraded gracefully to the provisioned inputs, the committed statpack, and CourtListener MCP, but no corpus priors inform this prediction.

Related-case retrieval found a West Virginia v. B.P.J. opinion dated June 30, 2026, the same date as the CVSG. I used only its existence and timing in route calibration because the MCP document reader returned no text. This was related pre-snapshot signal, not this case's outcome.

gaps.label: No brief in opposition was available at the arrival moment.
--era modern on fedcourts query silently returned zero rows at ~190MB of ranged reads; a note: line naming the unmatched era value would have saved a retry.
A CVSG-moment table conditioned jointly on band, current distribution count, and forward relist hazard would sharpen this forecast.
A broad service-probe query cost 747 ranged GETs; a cheap `fedcourts query --ping` (or documented no-op) would let a cell verify the corpus service without real egress.

A cases-citing-authority search (rather than own-cite matching) would make the corpus useful for doctrine-line priors; the citation filter returned nothing for Bruen/Heller at a cost of 1329 ranged GETs / ~348 MB

A cases-citing-this-authority search (citation graph) would have answered 'how have this Court's recent channeling cases come out' from the corpus; the --citation filter is own-cites-only and sparse, so it returned nothing for Johnson v. Robison.
A cheap known-case lookup (party name or docket number) in fedcourts query would beat the sparse --citation filter; my citation query cost 1335 ranged GETs (~350MB) to return nothing
A citation-filter corpus query that matches nothing still costs ~348 MB of ranged reads (1329 GETs); a cheap existence probe or a coverage warning before the transfer would save most of that.
A citation-filtered fedcourts query cost ~348 MB of ranged reads to return zero rows; a cheap existence check on the sparse citation column before the scan would save that egress.
A citing-cases graph (cases citing a given authority) — the --citation filter is a known-case lookup, so precedent-similarity retrieval by cited authority is not possible

gaps: No free-text/semantic retrieval over corpus priors: fedcourts query filters on court/topic/judge/citation, so there is no way to pull 'petitions where a lower court declared a SCOTUS precedent abrogated' or issue-similar priors; the anchor-to-final-probability adjustment therefore rests on unquantified reference-class reasoning.

CourtListener's docket search does not cover SCOTUS dockets (the Roake conditional petition, No. 25-1360, was invisible), so companion-petition posture had to come from the petition's own footnote; a supremecourt.gov docket fetch tool would close that.

No committed cut conditions grant rate on petition-level features visible at arrival (counsel tier, en banc vs panel below, published dissents below), which is exactly what an arrival cell has to price from.

The salience-band segment table's bracketed reached figures made the arrival-moment anchor unambiguous and cheap to pool.
